title: Route 53 DNS
description: Learn about hosted zones, DNS records, routing policies, and health checks in Amazon Route 53.

data.text: The Domain Name System (DNS) is the phonebook of the internet. It translates human-readable domain names like example.com into IP addresses that computers use to communicate. Amazon Route 53 is AWS's scalable and highly available DNS web service.

data.title: Why Route 53?
data.text: Route 53 connects user requests to AWS resources like EC2 instances, load balancers, and S3 buckets. It also provides health checking, traffic management, and domain registration.

A hosted zone is a container for DNS records for a domain. Each hosted zone has a set of name servers assigned by Route 53. You create DNS records inside the hosted zone to tell Route 53 how to route traffic for specific subdomains or the root domain.

data.text: Route 53 offers several routing policies that control how it responds to DNS queries. Simple routing returns one value. Weighted routing lets you distribute traffic across multiple resources based on assigned weights. Latency-based routing sends users to the Region with the lowest network latency. Geolocation routing directs users to specific endpoints based on their geographic location.

Route 53 health checks monitor the health and performance of your web applications and servers. When a health check detects that an endpoint is unhealthy, Route 53 can stop routing traffic to that endpoint. Health checks can check an endpoint, a CloudWatch alarm, or a combination of endpoints.

points: Route 53 is AWS's managed DNS service
